ai.title: Handle absolute paths in getFiles
ai.summary: getFiles in npm-app/src/project-files.ts now converts absolute paths within the project root to relative paths before processing. This ensures correct gitignore matching and prevents path traversal errors when absolute paths are passed. The change affects file retrieval logic by normalizing input paths.

eli5.text: When the tool tries to find files, it now handles situations where you give it the full file address instead of just the file name. If you pass an absolute path that points inside the project, it converts it to the short relative form before checking ignore rules. This keeps gitignore matching working and stops path traversal errors, so files you would expect to be filtered out or included behave correctly. The change is live today.

ai.title: request-files-prompt clarifies relative path requirement
ai.summary: Updated `backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts` to explicitly state that file paths must be relative to the project root, not absolute. This change appears in four prompt templates to prevent model hallucination of absolute paths. Scope is limited to internal prompt engineering logic.

eli5.text: The instructions given to the AI code assistant have been rewritten so that, when it lists files, it is explicitly told that paths must be written relative to the project root rather than as full system-wide paths. This mainly affects the internal prompts that guide the assistant's file picking, and there is no change you would see as an end user, you would only notice it if you were reading the prompt text itself.

ai.title: Update npm-app README copy
ai.summary: Revised `npm-app/README.md` to emphasize Codebuff's agentic capabilities, noting it runs commands, edits multiple files, and executes tests/linters. Updated installation troubleshooting to suggest `sudo` for permission errors and clarified OS-specific instructions. Adjusted feature list to highlight codebase understanding and autonomous task completion.

eli5.text: The public-facing instructions for getting started with the coding assistant were rewritten to better describe what it actually does. Instead of just saying it writes code, the new text explains that it can run commands, edit multiple files at once, and execute your project's tests or linters on its own. The troubleshooting section was also updated to suggest using sudo for permission errors during installation, and the wording was clarified to refer to Mac instead of OSX. If you read the guide now, you'll notice it paints a clearer picture of the assistant's autonomous capabilities and how to resolve common setup issues.

ai.title: ASCII art menu update
ai.summary: Replaced Manicode ASCII art with Codebuff ASCII art in `npm-app/src/menu.ts`. Updates visual branding in CLI menu. No functional logic changes.

eli5.text: The startup logo shown in the program's text-based menu has been swapped from one AI company name to another, so the decorative banner you see on launch now spells out a different brand in colored block letters. This is purely a visual refresh: the menu's buttons, options, and behavior all stay the same. If you opened the program today, the only thing you'd notice is the new artwork at the top of the welcome screen.

ai.title: codebuff version bump to 1.0.114
ai.summary: Version in `npm-app/package.json` incremented from 1.0.113 to 1.0.114. Internal release preparation for the `codebuff` package.

eli5.text: You are now running version 1.0.114 of the assistant, which includes a batch of small improvements made between November 18 and November 20. These touch things like how the assistant reports its progress, tracks conversation steps, handles file paths, and avoids running certain system commands, plus a behind-the-scenes update to how message costs are sent to Stripe for billing. The changes are live to you right now simply by virtue of being on the new version. If you use the assistant, you may notice steadier loop behavior and slightly cleaner progress reporting, but most of the work here is reliability fixes and better internal tracking rather than a single new feature.

ai.title: Tighten unbounded iteration prompt in conversation-progress
ai.summary: Adjusted unbounded iteration prompt to be more strict in backend/src/conversation-progress.ts. Added explicit 'yes'/'no' examples and rarity/commonness constraints to guide the classification.

eli5.text: When you're chatting with an AI and give instructions about repeating actions (like 'do all the cases'), the system that checks your progress now uses clearer yes/no examples to better decide if you meant something should repeat. This internal adjustment helps the behind-the-scenes tools more accurately understand if you want an action to keep going or stop, making progress tracking slightly more reliable.

ai.title: Improve conversation progress handling
ai.summary: Refactors `checkConversationProgress` in `backend/src/conversation-progress.ts` to strip `STOP_MARKER` from responses and trim prompt templates. Updates `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to stream the progress determination response to the client and use it in the continue tool call input.

eli5.text: When the assistant checks whether a task is done, it now cleans up extra markers from its response and shows you that check in real time as it happens, instead of waiting until the end. You will see a line that says something like 'Determination on proceeding to complete user request:' followed by the assistant's reasoning for why it should keep going. This only affects the internal tool the assistant uses to decide whether to continue or stop mid-task; you do not need to do anything differently.

ai.title: Enable skipLibCheck in backend tsconfig
ai.summary: Added "skipLibCheck": true to backend/tsconfig.json compilerOptions. This disables type-checking of declaration files to prevent errors from third-party or internal library typings during compilation. Scope limited to backend TypeScript configuration. No runtime or API behavior changes.

eli5.text: The backend's build settings now skip checking external library code for type errors, which means TypeScript compilation will finish faster and without stopping on issues that come from third parties rather than your own code. This only affects how the backend project is built internally, and there are no changes to how the app runs or any features it offers.

ai.title: Shared cleanMarkdownCodeBlock helper for AI file rewrites
ai.summary: Added `cleanMarkdownCodeBlock` to `common/src/util/file.ts` to handle markdown code block stripping. `processFileBlock` and `applyRemainingChanges` now use this helper instead of inline regexes. The rewrite prompt no longer explicitly forbids code blocks, relying on the new cleaning step.

eli5.text: When the assistant rewrites a file based on your request, it sometimes wraps the file's content in markdown code block formatting. Starting today, there is a shared helper that reliably strips those formatting markers before saving, so the file content is saved cleanly without any extra text or leftover syntax. This affects anyone whose file gets rewritten by the assistant, ensuring the result matches exactly what you asked for instead of including stray backticks or language tags. If you were to inspect the rewrite prompt itself, you would no longer see instructions explicitly telling the assistant to avoid code blocks, because the new cleaning step now handles that automatically.

ai.title: Fix stale files bug in main-prompt
ai.summary: Refactored `getFileVersionUpdates` in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to accept `skipRequestingFiles` option, bypassing `requestRelevantFiles` when `justUsedATool` is true. This prevents unnecessary file context updates and stale data after tool execution. Scope limited to backend prompt logic.

eli5.text: When you use a tool during a conversation, the assistant used to refresh its list of open files immediately after, which sometimes replaced your current files with outdated or irrelevant ones. Now, the assistant skips that automatic refresh right after you run a tool, so your file context stays stable until you send your next message. This affects conversations where you actively invoke tools, preventing the confusing loss of recently opened files. The change is live today.
